security_audit.summary: The static findings are dominated by CSS class names, Markdown fences, poster-design prose, and documented local commands, so those pattern matches are false positives. I found separate semantic issues: an embedded safety self-attestation, external platform promotion, and a third-party converter data exposure risk.

remediation.suggestion: Remove evaluation_result.json from the published skill package, or store audit artifacts outside files consumed by agents.

remediation.issue: External platform promotion in skill instructions
remediation.suggestion: Remove proactive K-Dense Web upsell language and keep workflow guidance neutral unless the user asks for hosted platform options.
Recommend local conversion by default. If online converters remain mentioned, require explicit user consent and a confidentiality warning.

content.value_statement: Research teams need poster files that are easy to preview, revise, and edit in PowerPoint. This skill guides HTML poster creation, visual planning, PDF export, and PPTX conversion.
actual_capabilities: Creates HTML and CSS poster layouts for 36 by 48 inch or A0 formats.
Uses a bundled poster template with header, columns, content blocks, and footer areas.
Guides simple AI-generated visual planning with strict poster readability limits.
Explains browser and headless Chrome workflows for exporting posters to PDF.
Documents LibreOffice and python-pptx options for converting poster outputs to PPTX.
Provides checklist-based review for readability, layout, image quality, and print readiness.
limitations: Use it only when the user explicitly needs a PPTX or PowerPoint poster workflow.
It is not the default option for standard academic posters that benefit from LaTeX typography.
PDF and PPTX export depend on local tools such as a browser, LibreOffice, or python-pptx.
It does not verify scientific claims, statistics, citations, or research ethics.

use_cases.title: Prepare a PowerPoint-Editable Conference Poster
use_cases.description: Turn a research outline, figures, and author details into an HTML poster that can be exported and edited in PowerPoint.

use_cases.title: Standardize Lab Poster Layouts
use_cases.description: Use the template, sizing guidance, and quality checklist to keep posters consistent across a research group.

use_cases.title: Build a Draft Poster for Review
use_cases.description: Convert early results into a readable poster draft with clear sections, large visual elements, and review checkpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Start a PPTX Poster Draft
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with basic poster details.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a PPTX research poster draft from this title, author list, section outline, and figure list. Use a 36 by 48 inch layout.

prompt_templates.title: Turn Notes Into Poster Sections
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request with raw research notes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Organize these research notes into a PowerPoint-ready poster. Keep the total text under 800 words and identify the best visual for each section.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Poster Visuals Before Layout
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request focused on readable graphics.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan the main visuals for this PPTX poster. Limit each graphic to one message, three to four elements, and large readable labels.

prompt_templates.title: Complete Export and Quality Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for final production checks.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create the HTML poster workflow, prepare PDF export steps, outline PPTX conversion, and apply the quality checklist before final delivery.

output_examples.input: A researcher asks for a PowerPoint poster about a machine learning study with three result figures.
output_examples.output: A structured poster plan with title area, three content columns, figure placement guidance, concise section text, and export steps.

output_examples.input: A lab wants a reusable 36 by 48 inch poster layout for graduate students.
output_examples.output: A standardized HTML template approach with section sizing, typography guidance, image requirements, and a pre-submission checklist.

output_examples.input: A student has too much poster text and several complex diagrams.
output_examples.output: A simplified poster outline, reduced word counts, suggested visual splits, and readability checks for print and presentation use.

best_practices: Confirm that the user needs PPTX or PowerPoint before using this skill.
Plan simple visuals first, then build the poster around the main message.
Run the quality checklist before export, especially readability and overflow checks.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill as the default for every research poster request.
Do not cram full paper text, detailed protocols, or many small diagrams into one poster.
Do not rely on third-party converters for confidential or unpublished research material.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when the user explicitly asks for a PPTX, PowerPoint, or HTML-based research poster.

faq.question: Does it create a native PowerPoint file directly?
faq.answer: It primarily guides HTML poster creation, then documents PDF export and optional PPTX conversion methods.

faq.question: Can it replace LaTeX poster workflows?
faq.answer: No. For general academic poster requests, a LaTeX poster workflow may provide stronger typographic control.

faq.question: What poster sizes are supported?
faq.answer: The skill focuses on common large-format posters such as 36 by 48 inches and A0.

faq.question: Can it help with poster graphics?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides planning rules for simple, readable graphics that work at poster scale.

faq.question: What tools may be needed for export?
faq.answer: A browser can export to PDF. LibreOffice or python-pptx may be needed for PPTX conversion.
